QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_48

question.text: Under SAS-500 an SE reports 'soil organic carbon (SOC) improved by 15%'. The SIA should INSIST on:

answer.text: Soil-lab test results (Walkley-Black or dry-combustion method) at baseline and endline, on GPS-tagged fixed plots, with same-laboratory analysis for comparability

explanation.text: The Logic: Soil organic carbon is a laboratory parameter, conventionally measured by methods such as Walkley-Black or dry-combustion. Defensible evidence for a percentage improvement requires baseline and end-line lab tests on GPS-tagged fixed plots, analysed in the same laboratory to control for methodological drift. This is the kind of evidence sufficient and valid enough to support a soil-quality improvement claim. The Trap: Options A, B and C — trusting the SE estimate, relying on satellite imagery alone, or relying on a farmer's opinion — are either non-measurable or single-source and cannot evidence a quantitative SOC change. Note: The cited SIA workbook supports general baseline/end-line data, evidence sufficiency, validity, and environmental/soil-quality indicators under IWMP-style programmes, but does not specifically mention SOC, Walkley-Black, dry-combustion, GPS-tagged fixed plots, or same-laboratory comparability. The framing above reflects general agronomic measurement practice rather than a workbook-page citation.
